html:
The Oslo Accords were agreements between Israel and the PLO, worked out in secret talks in Norway. The first was signed at the White House on 13 September 1993, sealed by a handshake between Yitzhak Rabin and Yasser Arafat.

The PLO recognised Israel, and Israel recognised the PLO as the voice of the Palestinians. A Palestinian Authority was set up to govern parts of Gaza and the West Bank, while the hardest questions, borders, Jerusalem, refugees and settlements, were left for later talks. A second accord in 1995 split the West Bank into zones.

Rabin was shot dead by a Jewish extremist in November 1995, and Hamas bombings and growing settlements eroded trust. Final talks failed at Camp David in 2000, and the Second Intifada followed. See also First Intifada.
sum: The Oslo Accords were agreements between Israel and the PLO, worked out in secret talks in Norway. The first was signed at the White House on 13 September 1993, sealed by a handshake between Yitzhak Rabin and Yasser Arafat.
